findings.body: The SMS scheduler's deleteMany OR-branch deletes every workflow reminder with retryCount > 1 irrespective of method, so non-SMS reminders could be silently removed if that shared column is ever incremented elsewhere.
findings.failure_mode: Deletion query matches broader rows than intended, risking data loss of unrelated reminders.
findings.impact: The SMS scheduler's deleteMany OR-branch deletes every workflow reminder with retryCount > 1 irrespective of method, so non-SMS reminders could be silently removed if that shared column is ever incremented elsewhere.
findings.root_cause: The second OR condition added to deleteMany omits the method filter present in the first branch, treating the shared retryCount column as SMS-specific.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount OR-branch so the retry-based deletion only targets SMS reminders.
findings.title: retryCount deletion filter not scoped to SMS method
findings.trigger: Any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or seat/mandatory reminders) whose shared retryCount column ever reaches a value greater than 1 while the SMS cron runs.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R38-R42 add an OR branch with only `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` and no `method` filter. The first OR branch correctly scopes to SMS, but the second branch will match any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method (EMAIL, etc.). This is a real defect introduced by the patch.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Right now when SMS fails to send because of whatever reason (e.g. invalid phone number), we are trying to keep scheduling it in our corn job until the date is reached. This PR introduces a retry count, after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder.
pr.title: fix: add retryCount to workflowReminder

raw_findings.root_cause: The second OR condition added to deleteMany omits the method filter present in the first branch, treating the shared retryCount column as SMS-specific.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount OR-branch so the retry-based deletion only targets SMS reminders.
raw_findings.title: retryCount deletion filter not scoped to SMS method
raw_findings.trigger: Any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or seat/mandatory reminders) whose shared retryCount column ever reaches a value greater than 1 while the SMS cron runs.

raw_findings.body: Neither the else branch nor the catch executes, so retryCount stays unchanged and the reminder is re-fetched every cron run without ever reaching the retryCount>1 deletion threshold, only cleaned up once scheduledDate passes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Retry-cap fix does not cover all non-schedulable reminders.
raw_findings.impact: Neither the else branch nor the catch executes, so retryCount stays unchanged and the reminder is re-fetched every cron run without ever reaching the retryCount>1 deletion threshold, only cleaned up once scheduledDate passes.
raw_findings.root_cause: The retry increment is placed only inside the message/sendTo guarded block, leaving the no-message/no-sendTo path uncounted.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Increment retryCount (or otherwise handle) reminders that fall through the message/sendTo guard so they are also bounded by the retry limit.
raw_findings.title: retryCount never incremented when no message or sendTo
raw_findings.trigger: A reminder whose computed message is empty or whose sendTo is falsy, so the outer `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` is false and no throw occurs.

raw_findings.body: Both runs read the same stale retryCount and write the same value, losing an increment so a persistently failing reminder is retried more times than intended before deletion.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Lost updates under concurrent cron execution.
raw_findings.impact: Both runs read the same stale retryCount and write the same value, losing an increment so a persistently failing reminder is retried more times than intended before deletion.
raw_findings.root_cause: The increment is computed from the previously fetched in-memory value rather than an atomic database increment.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use Prisma's atomic update `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` instead of computing from the read value.
raw_findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of retryCount
raw_findings.trigger: Two overlapping executions of the SMS cron (e.g., a slow run not finished before the next scheduled run) processing the same reminder.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the retry threshold (e.g., off-by-one in `gt: 1`) or increment placement would go undetected by CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Absence of tests leaves the new control-flow unverified.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the retry threshold (e.g., off-by-one in `gt: 1`) or increment placement would go undetected by CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: New retry/delete behavior is introduced without accompanying tests.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit/integration test that simulates scheduleSMS failure and verifies retryCount is incremented and that reminders exceeding the retry limit are deleted.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for retryCount increment and deletion behavior
raw_findings.trigger: Merging the retry logic without any test asserting that a failed schedule increments retryCount and that reminders with retryCount>1 are deleted.

finding.trigger: A reminder whose computed message is empty or whose sendTo is falsy, so the outer `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` is false and no throw occurs.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim is that retryCount is never incremented when message/sendTo is falsy. However, the loop only processes reminders fetched with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (line 50), so only SMS reminders are processed. If message/sendTo is falsy, the reminder simply isn't scheduled this run and will be retried next cron. This is expected behavior for a retry mechanism, not a bug - the reminder will eventually be cleaned up by scheduledDate passing. The finding mischaracterizes normal retry semantics.

finding.verifier_reason: While technically true that `reminder.retryCount + 1` is a read-modify-write pattern, the trigger requires overlapping cron executions processing the same reminder. The finding is speculative about concurrent execution without evidence this is a realistic scenario in this codebase.
